text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - Parliament on Thursday approved a law banning privatisation of the second terrestrial channel of the official Slovak Television. The law was presented by the opposition Party of the Democratic Left (SDL).
- President Michal Kovac has rejected a proposal by Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar to shorten the president's term in office as incompetent and single-purpose attempt aimed at ousting the president.

- Meciar said there was no reason to meet his Czech counterpart Vaclav Klaus since the current Czech political situation has made it impossible for Klaus to conclude any agreements aimed at solving problems in mutual relations.
- Energy prices for corporate customers will increase by some 10 percent from around mid-July, Meciar said.
- Parliamentary deputies of the ruling coalition have strictly rejected European Union criticism of a controversial Slovak history book as incompetent.
PRAVDA - Meciar said Slovakia's GDP should grow by some five to six percent year-on-year this year and next year.
- He also said Slovakia was preparing a law that should increase the minimum sum required as basic capital of a limited liability company to 500,000 crowns from the current 100,000 crowns.
- Slovakia's sole refiner Slovnaft has processed 2.1 million tonnes of crude oil in the first five months of the year.
SME - Five main opposition parties are expected to approve an agreement on the creation of a pre-election coalition next weekend.

- The Ministry of Education said it would only accept final school certificates in Slovak and that it would impose sanctions on those schools and teachers which would hand out certificates in languages other than Slovak.
